cards.identity: Natural seed extract diluted in DPG; not isolated ambrettolide. Botanical/lot composition is not established by the generic CAS label.
cards.odor_role: Musky seed warmth with woody, hay, tobacco and wine-like facets. A source of natural texture and soft complexity, rather than a neutral clean-musk replacement.
cards.performance: The supplier's parent extract and other manufacturers support a persistent musky role qualitatively; the exact purchased dilution has no verified skin-longevity curve.
cards.handling: Keep the original dilution identity. Colour, viscosity, solubility and constituent allergens depend on the extract; the captured SDS has no usable classification data.
cards.lhomme: Possible later natural-texture comparison, but the seed/hay facets could move the clean sporty identity. Do not substitute it numerically for ambrettolide.
cards.name: Ambrette Seed Absolute 10% in DPG

cards.identity: Habanolide, CAS 111879-80-2; a macrocyclic musk lactone. The supplier lists a liquid.
cards.odor_role: Clean, diffusive musk with a warm, slightly woody underpinning. Its distinct task would be a dry, clear musky support behind the citrus and pepper.
cards.performance: Firmenich describes a powerful heart/base musk and reports two weeks on a smelling strip. That is manufacturer strip evidence, not two weeks on skin or proof of a more separated opening.
cards.handling: The supplier SDS flags aquatic hazards. Evaluate its own odor character; adding more powerful musk can also increase the perceived base presence.
cards.lhomme: A useful alternative-musks lane for a fresh rebuild, with the rest of the formula held constant. It is not established as an improvement over the original musk system.
cards.name: Habanolide

cards.identity: Helvetolide, CAS 141773-73-1; an alicyclic musk, distinct from Habanolide and Romandolide.
cards.odor_role: Musky warmth with pear-like freshness and ambrette facets. Its role is a fruity musky connection from opening through drydown.
cards.performance: The manufacturer specifically describes presence in the top note as well as later stages. 'Musk' therefore does not imply that it is absent from the initial spray.
cards.handling: The supplier SDS flags chronic aquatic toxicity. Pear/ambrette character must be assessed as part of the intended smell, not treated as an odorless performance aid.
cards.lhomme: Useful only if its fruity softness supports the original. Less conservative than a musk without a noticeable pear facet when preserving pink pepper is the goal.
cards.name: Helvetolide

cards.identity: Romandolide, CAS 236391-76-7; an alicyclic musk, not a polycyclic musk.
cards.odor_role: Soft musk with delicate balsamic facets. The manufacturer describes it as less fruity and less ambrette-like than Helvetolide, with more drydown volume.
cards.performance: It is described as both a top-note musk and a contributor to tenacity. Neither description proves that it will unmask pepper in this perfume.
cards.handling: The supplier SDS flags chronic aquatic toxicity. Supplier descriptions of airy or transparent character are sensory guidance, not measurements of reduced mixture masking.
cards.lhomme: A sensible controlled alternative to assess against the original musk system. Do not assume equal mass gives the same odor strength or that Galaxolide caused the block.
cards.name: Romandolide

cards.identity: Zenolide, CAS 54982-83-1; a macrocyclic diester musk.
cards.odor_role: Soft, delicate musk with red-fruit facets. Its role would be gentle musky body with a fruit-tinted texture.
cards.performance: IFF rates heart impact medium and base impact low. The supplier's long strip-life claim is a different endpoint and does not make Zenolide a proven high-projection base.
cards.handling: The live supplier SDS flags acute and chronic aquatic toxicity. The page was recovered after the local crawl missed it; its classification is recorded as a supplier statement, not a final safety assessment.
cards.lhomme: A worthwhile later musk alternative if the red-fruit nuance fits. It cannot be promised as a longevity-equivalent replacement.
issues: Supplier and manufacturer describe different performance endpoints
cards.name: Zenolide

cards.identity: Ambrofix, CAS 6790-58-5; an ambroxide material supplied as crystals. It is distinct from Ambrocenide.
cards.odor_role: Persistent ambergris-like warmth and woody body. Its specific job is the recognizable ambergris foundation, rather than a sharp woody booster.
cards.performance: Givaudan describes strong substantivity and stability. The supplier page contains conflicting strip-duration claims, so no numerical duration is accepted here.
cards.handling: Weigh crystals; a crystalline raw material is not a directly pipettable liquid. Any later stock preparation needs an explicit concentration and carrier.
cards.lhomme: First check overlap with the existing Ambrox component. This may be a grade comparison rather than a new functional role; extra Ambrofix would also change total amber loading.

cards.performance: IFF describes diffusion and substantivity above 48 hours in its ingredient compendium; the substrate/protocol is not a finished-perfume wear trial.
cards.handling: Supplier SDS flags sensitization and aquatic hazards. Its dry wood odor is an active character contribution, not an inert fixative.
cards.lhomme: Potentially compatible with a restrained dry woody heart, but an addition could make the opening woodier. Consider only for an identified missing woody role.

cards.identity: Birch tar oil rectified, nominal 10% in DPG. Rectified and crude birch pyrolysates require different treatment.
cards.odor_role: Intense smoke, phenolic leather and burnt wood. Useful when a deliberate smoky leather accent is required.
cards.performance: A character-dominant accent; there is no evidence it would recover a clean sporty opening or preserve the original smell.
cards.handling: IFRA distinguishes prohibited crude pyrolysate from rectified oils meeting PAH specifications. 'Rectified' on the name alone does not prove this lot meets those specifications.
cards.lhomme: Poor first candidate for this brief because smoke and leather introduce a conspicuous new direction.
cards.name: Birch Tar Oil Rectified 10% in DPG

issues: Historical trade name can mislead chemical-class assignment

overview.title: Research review of all 53 received PerfumersWorld stocks
overview.subtitle: Roles, odor character, evidence limits, handling and relevance to Chimie L’Homme
overview.scope: All 53 purchase lines from order 261004-055451ce1; 52 catalogue identities because Buccoxime was bought at two strengths.
summary: The collection expands the palette in several genuinely different directions: clean musks; dry woods and ambergris; citrus-to-floral materials; green/fruit accents; creamy lactones; natural extracts; and sweet/spicy character materials.

For the original L’Homme, the most useful first question remains the balance and character of its musk system. Habanolide and Romandolide are distinct comparison options. This review does not demonstrate that Galaxolide caused the block or that replacing it will preserve the original smell.

Florol, Magnolan and ethyl linalyl acetate offer different ways to connect fresh top notes to the heart. Their documented descriptions support separate hypotheses, not a combined addition or a claim that they physically separate odors.
Ambrocenide is an odor-active woody-amber booster, including in the opening. The manufacturer's 10% DPG sheet cannot supply quantitative properties or dosing for your 10% TEC bottle.
Many new materials would be excellent for other briefs but introduce a new recognizer into L’Homme: peach/coconut, apple/pineapple/cassis, tea/tobacco, smoky leather, saffron, maple or vanilla.
boundaries: Received masses are the purchase quantities confirmed by the user, not current remaining inventory or active chemical masses.
Nominal 10% and 85% preparations retain an unspecified percentage basis. 'As supplied' records whole-product loading, not a purity assay.

Odor character and common roles are sourced primarily from the supplier's own descriptions and manufacturer technical literature. The proposed role in L’Homme is the reviewer's untested formulation hypothesis.
Strip persistence, stability in a product base, diffusion descriptions, vapor pressure, and wearer-observed longevity are different endpoints. No 6-hour skin-performance guarantee is inferred.
No complete lot-specific composition, safety assessment, IFRA compliance calculation, numerical OAV model or dosing card was produced. Missing or contradictory quantitative data remain unresolved.

Research collection is complete for the 53-item scope; scientific and regulatory evidence depth varies by material. No runtime physics, odor-threshold values, inventory authorities or formulas were changed by this research.

key_findings.title: Both Buccoxime purchases are the same odorant in different preparations
key_findings.text: Keep the undiluted crystals and 10% DPG stock separate in dosing records. They do not supply two complementary musk or fruit roles.

key_findings.title: Three misleading historical trade names
key_findings.text: C-14 and C-18 'aldehydes' are lactones. The supplier's Maple Lactone CAS identifies cyclotene, a hydroxyketone. The latter also has an unresolved physical-form discrepancy.

key_findings.title: Fructone B is not ordinary Fructone
key_findings.text: The supplier's 6290-17-1 identity matches IFF Fraistone. IFF Fructone is 6413-10-1. Formula aliases must preserve the difference.

key_findings.title: Natural preparations are whole products
key_findings.text: Ambrette absolute is not ambrettolide; vanilla absolute is not vanillin; orris butter is not an irone assay; lavandin absolute is not lavandin essential oil.

key_findings.title: Terpeneless lemon is not an FCF declaration
key_findings.text: The retrieved lemon document lacks usable composition/classification data. Its name alone does not resolve furocoumarins or phototoxicity.

key_findings.title: Supplier document presence is not proof of suitability
key_findings.text: Several retrieved SDS pages contain no classification data, and some pages have contradictory physical or hazard entries. Generic conformity tables were not promoted into material-specific safe-use limits.

key_findings.title: Published restrictions and grade specifications matter
key_findings.text: Coumarin, rose ketones, phenylacetaldehyde and Safranal have relevant published IFRA restrictions. Rectified birch tar must be distinguished from prohibited crude pyrolysate and requires the applicable PAH specification.

lhomme_comparisons.question: Does changing one defined musk role improve citrus/pink-pepper clarity while preserving the original drydown?
lhomme_comparisons.caution: Compare alternatives separately; no equal-strength replacement factor was established.

lhomme_comparisons.question: Would a softer fruit-tinted musk texture help?
lhomme_comparisons.caution: Red-fruit or pear/ambrette facets can change the original smell.

lhomme_comparisons.materials: Florol, Magnolan, or ethyl linalyl acetate
lhomme_comparisons.question: Is there a missing transition between the fresh opening and the restrained heart?
lhomme_comparisons.caution: Each supplies its own floral/citrus character; adding all three confounds the question.

lhomme_comparisons.question: What happens when a distinct woody-amber booster is introduced?
lhomme_comparisons.caution: An addition to an old aliquot tests an addition, not replacement of its existing superamber.

lhomme_comparisons.materials: Ambrofix, Vertofix, Kephalis or cedryl acetate
lhomme_comparisons.question: Does the base need a different texture rather than more power?
lhomme_comparisons.caution: These have separate ambergris, cedar and tobacco/amber roles; they are not interchangeable fixatives.

evidence_notes.title: What the sensory literature supports
evidence_notes.text: Zak and colleagues measured nonlinear, antagonistic responses to odor mixtures in olfactory sensory neurons in freely breathing mice. This supports caution about predicting a mixture by adding individual material descriptions. It does not identify a culprit in L’Homme or demonstrate a human hedonic benefit from any replacement.

evidence_notes.title: IFRA status checked on 7 October 2026
evidence_notes.text: The public documentation located includes the 51st Amendment. IFRA reported that the 52nd consultation closed in June 2026, with formal notification expected towards late November 2026, and published an end-of-consultation update in August. Forthcoming changes are not treated as already-notified limits.

evidence_notes.title: Manufacturer and purchased grade
evidence_notes.text: The manufacturer sources describe their own grades. Agreement of a trade name/CAS supports identity-level interpretation, but does not prove the rebottled supplier's producer, assay or lot composition. The Ambrocenide DPG-to-TEC and Ambrette extract comparisons are explicitly limited.

evidence_notes.title: Handling and storage
evidence_notes.text: Retain original labels and carriers, close containers promptly, and follow the exact product SDS for storage and handling. Use mass for solids and confirm any future dilution is homogeneous. No universal refrigeration temperature, shelf-life, dissolution procedure or safe skin-evaluation concentration is inferred for the entire collection.
